title: The pullback of a finite type module is of finite type
statement: Let $f:X\to Y$ be a morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme] and let $\mathcal G$ be an $\mathcal O_Y$-module of finite type [pqf-def-coherent], i.e. every point of $Y$ has an open neighbourhood $V$ with a surjection $\mathcal O_V^{\oplus n}\twoheadrightarrow\mathcal G|_V$ for some $n\ge0$. Then the pullback $f^*\mathcal G$ [def-pc-module-pullback] is an $\mathcal O_X$-module of finite type: every point of $X$ has an open neighbourhood $U$ with a surjection $\mathcal O_U^{\oplus n}\twoheadrightarrow(f^*\mathcal G)|_U$ (one may take $U=f^{-1}V$ and the same $n$ as for $\mathcal G$ on $V$).

source.place: Sheaves of Modules (modules.tex), Lemma 01B6 (lemma-pullback-finite-type), stated there for a morphism of ringed spaces; its proof uses that $f^*$ is right exact and commutes with direct sums (Lemma 01AJ, lemma-exactness-pushforward-pullback), $f^*\mathcal O_Y=\mathcal O_X$, and that pullback commutes with restriction to opens (argument of Lemma 01B3, lemma-pullback-locally-generated)

proof.text: For an open V of Y put U = f^{-1}V and let f′: U → V be the restricted scheme morphism. The equivalences overEquiv V and overEquiv U identify modules on the over sites with modules on the open subschemes. Form F = (overEquiv V).functor followed by the Mathlib scheme-module pullback along f′ and (overEquiv U).inverse. The restriction-pullback isomorphisms, pullback composition and the equation U.ι ≫ f = f′ ≫ V.ι give F(G.over V) ≅ (pullback f G).over U. Uniqueness of left adjoints, using nonempty_tensorPullbackAdjunction f, replaces pullback f by tensorPullback f.

F preserves colimits and epimorphisms, since its outer functors are equivalences and its middle functor is a left adjoint. The Mathlib pullbackObjUnitToUnit is an isomorphism because the preimage functor on opens is final. Together with sheafOfModulesEquivOverUnit and sheafOfModulesEquivOverInverseUnit this gives unit over U ≅ F(unit over V). Mathlib mapFreeIso then identifies the free sheaf on ULift(Fin n) over U with F applied to the free sheaf with the same index over V. Compose that isomorphism, F.map φ, and the comparison of the previous step. This composite is epi for every epi φ, establishing the second conjunct without a finite-type assumption.

Take finite local generators data q for G. For each i, give the finite index type (q.generators i).I a Fintype instance and identify it with ULift(Fin n) using equivFin and ulift. The freeFunctor map of this equivalence composed with the generating epimorphism is an epi φ on q.X i. Apply the second conjunct just proved to obtain an epi ψ on f^{-1}(q.X i) with the same finite rank. Its freeHomEquiv image supplies generating sections.

The inverse-image opens form a cover: for x in an arbitrary open W of X, the cover q at f(x) supplies an open V containing f(x) and a map V → q.X i. Intersect W with f^{-1}V to obtain a covering-sieve member mapping to f^{-1}(q.X i) and containing x. Thus the constructed local generators data p cover the terminal object; all its generating index types ULift(Fin n) are finite. Apply IsFiniteType.mk to p and its finite-type proof and pair the result with the already proved local epi assertion. Empty opens and n = 0 need no exceptional case.
